items.name: Rainforest Gallery and Mt Donna Buang, Yarra Ranges NP
items.when: Any day (a cool-weather escape on hot days)
items.venue: Acheron Way / Donna Buang Rd, above Warburton
items.note: A 40 m elevated walkway 15 m above cool temperate rainforest, with Mountain Ash and Myrtle Beech up to 400 years old, plus a 20-minute stair walk along Cement Creek; then the 1.2 km-high summit lookout. Check the fire danger rating before heading to the ranges.

items.name: Warburton Redwood Forest and Cement Creek loop
items.when: Any day; go mid-week or early to beat crowds
items.note: Over 1,470 Californian redwoods, planted in the 1930s and now 55 m tall, in shady rows; loop down to the Yarra through ferns, or do the 16 km return O'Shannassy Aqueduct Trail from Yuonga Rd. Shade makes it a good warm-day pick.

items.name: Two Bays Walking Trail, Mornington Peninsula
items.when: Any day (do a section, or all 26 km in long summer daylight)
items.venue: Dromana to Cape Schanck (about 60 km from Melbourne)
items.note: Blue-wren-signed trail from Arthurs Seat's steep gravel climbs through Greens Bush to the Cape Schanck cliffs; carry plenty of water and start early on warm days.

items.name: Darby River to Tongue Point, Wilsons Promontory NP
items.venue: Darby River carpark, Wilsons Prom (about 3 hrs from Melbourne)
items.note: A coastal walk over an ancient dune and granite-studded heath to Tongue Point, with a detour to sheltered Fairy Cove for a swim; wallabies are common. A summer day trip or weekend away.

items.name: Arthurs Seat State Park mountain bike trails
items.venue: Seawinds, Upper or Hillview (Dromana) carparks, Arthurs Seat
items.note: Over 25 km of singletrack and management tracks on steep rocky terrain, for all abilities; Hillview has water and a bike repair station, the others need your own water.

items.name: Forrest Mountain Bike Trails, Great Otway NP
items.note: About 70 km of singletrack and new flow trails through tall eucalypts, native bush and fern gullies, from a small-town base; the Otways' cool forest suits early summer.

items.name: Port Fairy Rail Trail
items.venue: Warrnambool to Port Fairy (about 260 km SW of Melbourne)
items.note: 38 km of asphalt and fine gravel past Koroit and Tower Hill to Port Fairy, about two hours' brisk riding; pair it with a Great Ocean Road summer weekend.

items.name: East Gippsland Rail Trail
items.venue: Bairnsdale to Orbost (about 280 km east of Melbourne)
items.note: 96 km through farmland and forest with old trestle bridges and Gippsland Lakes glimpses, ending at the long Snowy River trestle; good as a multi-day summer tour.

items.name: TISM, The Bamboos (with Tim Rogers and WILSN) and Automatic: 3RRR 50th birthday show
items.note: This Saturday: Triple R's second free birthday concert, led by masked Melbourne cult heroes TISM. Same day as the state election, so vote first.

items.name: Ann Wilson & Tripsitter: The Voice of Heart, with Dragon
items.note: News: it's this Sunday. Heart's Rock and Roll Hall of Fame singer plays the Heart classics, with Dragon (April Sun in Cuba) opening; tickets still on sale.

items.name: Live at the Gardens: SIX60, DMA'S and Cat Power
items.when: Fri 27 Nov (SIX60), Sat 28 Nov (DMA'S), Thu 3 Dec (Cat Power)
items.venue: Observatory Lawn, Royal Botanic Gardens Melbourne
items.note: The open-air series starts tomorrow: final tickets for SIX60 and DMA'S, and Cat Power plays her album The Greatest in full for its 20th anniversary.

items.name: The Dandy Warhols
items.note: The cult Portland alt-rockers (Bohemian Like You) touring their new covers album Pin Ups, with Nice Biscuit supporting.

items.name: Jimmy Eat World: Bleed American 25th Anniversary Tour
items.note: The 2001 album behind The Middle and Sweetness, played for its 25th anniversary.

items.name: Vision Australia's Carols by Candlelight
items.price: GA $88 adult, $189 family; rehearsal GA from $41
items.note: Melbourne's Christmas Eve tradition, live from the Bowl; the cheaper rehearsal night is a relaxed way to go with kids.

items.name: Billy Idol: It's A Nice Day To... Tour Again!
items.note: Just announced: his first Australian tour since 2020, opening in Melbourne, weeks after his Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction. Live Nation presale today, general sale tomorrow (Fri 27 Nov) 11am.

items.name: The Jacksons
items.note: Original Jackson 5 members Jackie and Marlon play I Want You Back, ABC and Blame It on the Boogie, their first Australian visit since 2019; on sale now.

items.name: Smokie (UK): Greatest Hits Tour
items.note: The 70s soft-rock band of Living Next Door to Alice and Lay Back in the Arms of Someone, a huge seller in Australia; on sale now.

items.name: Mental As Anything with the Berserk Warriors Orchestra
items.venue: Ian Potter State Theatre, Arts Centre Melbourne
items.note: Two world-premiere shows of Live It Up and other hits with a 35-piece orchestra, arranged by The Cat Empire's Roscoe James Irwin; tickets from today (Thu 26 Nov) via Arts Centre Melbourne.

items.name: Ronan Keating: Just Getting Started World Tour
items.note: Boyzone classics and solo hits like When You Say Nothing At All.

items.name: Brooks & Dunn: Neon Moon Tour 2027
items.note: The country duo with Ashley McBryde and Mack Geiger; on sale now.

items.name: Hasan Hates Ronny | Ronny Hates Hasan (Hasan Minhaj and Ronny Chieng)
items.when: Sat 19 Dec: new earlier show (doors 4pm) plus 8pm show
items.note: News: a second, earlier show has been added on the day. The Daily Show alumni stage a 'debate to the death' about America and each other; MA15+.

items.name: Adam Kay: 'Twas the Nightshift Before Christmas
items.note: The ex-doctor behind This Is Going to Hurt, with festive tales from hospital night shifts; tickets still available for Melbourne.

items.name: Melbourne International Comedy Festival: Opening Night Allstars Supershow
items.note: Just announced: local legends and international headliners in one filmed show that kicks off the 2027 festival; 16+.

items.name: Jameela Jamil: Prison of Perfection
items.note: The Good Place's Tahani in a live show on perfectionism and fame, with a special guest and Q&A; more conversation than straight stand-up.

items.name: Lucy Darling: Cheers, with Tom Cardy
items.note: Just announced: Carisa Hendrix's cocktail-sipping socialite mixes quick wit and magic, joined by musical comic Tom Cardy.

items.name: Australian Open 2027 and the Million-Dollar AO 1 Point Slam
items.when: 11–31 Jan 2027; 1 Point Slam final Wed 13 Jan
items.price: Opening Week adults $10, kids $5 (free on day one); 1 Point Slam from $59
items.note: News: early-bird Ground Pass pricing ends Mon 30 Nov. Sinner, Alcaraz, Gauff and Osaka are signed up for the 1 Point Slam at Rod Laver Arena.

items.name: BBL|16 Melbourne Derbies at the MCG: Stars v Renegades
items.when: Mon 4 Jan, 6:05pm (and Renegades v Stars Sat 16 Jan, 7:15pm)
items.note: Both cross-town Big Bash derbies are at the 'G in January school holidays; on sale now via Ticketek.

items.name: Boomers v Iran and v Jordan (FIBA World Cup 2027 qualifiers)
items.note: No NBL games in Melbourne this weekend because of the FIBA window. The 8–0 Boomers need one win to reach Qatar 2027; United's Tom Wilson is in the squad.

items.name: Melbourne United v Brisbane Bullets
items.note: News: United's first home game after the FIBA break, billed as the Member Appreciation Game; they are 9–6.

items.name: Melbourne United v Cairns Taipans (Open Air Game)
items.note: News: billed as the 'original and best Open Air Game' (an Ignite Cup game), a pre-Christmas summer-evening one.

items.name: SE Melbourne Phoenix January home games
items.when: Wed 6 Jan 5:30pm (v Tasmania), Sun 10 Jan 3pm (v NZ Breakers), Thu 21 Jan 7:30pm (v Adelaide), Sun 24 Jan 5pm (v Perth)
items.note: All four January games are at the Phoenix's 'Heartland' venue while the Australian Open takes over Melbourne Park; good school-holiday outings, on sale now.

items.name: Melbourne United in Bendigo
items.when: Thu 7 Jan, 7:30pm (v Adelaide, Pride Round) & Wed 20 Jan, 5:30pm (v Tasmania)
items.note: United's January home games are in Bendigo while the Australian Open is on; pair one with a holiday day trip.

items.name: The Live Aid Musical: Just For One Day
items.note: The story of the 1985 concert 'the day rock 'n' roll changed the world', the one with Queen, Bowie and Sting; join the waitlist for first access.

items.name: Fiddler on the Roof
items.note: News: final month of the season. Tevye, Anatevka and 'Tradition', a good pick for a family night out before it closes.

items.name: Disney's The Lion King
items.note: The Broadway spectacle returns to Melbourne; tickets on sale through Marriner Group, with no transaction fees.

items.name: Private Lives
items.note: Hugh Bonneville (Downton Abbey) and Lisa McCune in Noël Coward's sparkling comedy of divorced lovers.

items.name: Dinosaur World Live
items.price: Save $5 a ticket on 4 or more
items.note: A 50-minute school-holiday show of giant dinosaur puppets, ages 3 and up.

items.name: Barbie: The Exhibition
items.note: News: opens this Saturday. 250+ dolls from London's Design Museum, including the 1959 Number 1 Barbie and the 1962 Dreamhouse; low-sensory sessions from 3 Dec.

items.name: David Bowie: Southern Moonlight by Denis O'Regan
items.note: Just announced: never-before-seen tour photos, including rare Australian moments, from Bowie's long-time photographer, marking his 80th birthday; a four-day pop-up.

items.name: Colour: See the World in a New Light
items.note: Hands-on Questacon exhibition with 21 exhibits on colour, light and illusions, aimed at ages 5–14; in its final summer, a good school-holiday visit.

items.name: Myer Christmas Windows: Toy Story
items.note: The 71st season brings Pixar's Merry Christmas Woody to life across six windows.

items.name: Chanukah: Pillars of Light 2026
items.when: Fri 4 – Fri 11 Dec (evenings; no event Sat 5 Dec)
items.note: The Ark Centre's week-long Chanukah festival, with Deborah Conway and Willy Zygier (4 Dec), the MSO with the Lamm Jewish Library (8 Dec) and klezmer (9 Dec).

items.name: Melbourne Makers' Market and St Paul's Market
items.venue: City Square and St Paul's Cathedral (Swanston St)
items.note: This Saturday: two curated 40-maker art and design markets a block apart, handy for early Christmas gifts.

items.name: Christmas Square
items.note: Opens tomorrow: the 17.5 m tree with light and sound shows and glowing bell swings (no tree shows Sat 28 Nov).

items.name: Heide Market
items.venue: Heide Museum of Modern Art, Bulleen
items.note: Over 120 makers in Heide's sculpture park and gardens; combine it with the Love Letters exhibition inside.

items.name: Christmas Carnival
items.price: Free entry; rides $8 kids, from $12 adults
items.note: Ferris wheel, dodgems and the 60 m Sky Flyer XXL by the river, with carnival food.

items.name: Coburg Night Market
items.note: Three summer nights of street food from 25 vendors, 40+ local makers, live music and kids' workshops.
